oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: SLO breach detected for /v1/generate (hosted/runtime-pool-us-east-1). p95=0.92s p99=2.42s (SLO 1.5s). kv_cache_evictions_total spiked ~4200 in last 5m, kv_cache_hit_ratio dropped from 0.92 -> 0.74. Triggering page to runtime oncall.

Maria Garcia: I'm up. Thanks bot. I see multiple streaming stalls reported by clients (stall > 5s). Any known deploys?

Sam Kim: no deploys in last 30m from release bot. I'll pull metrics and logs.

Sam Kim: quick metrics snapshot:```
# metrics snapshot (us-east-1)
kv_cache_items_total 1.2e6
kv_cache_evictions_total 4.2e3 (5m)
kv_cache_prefill_ops 1.1e4
kv_cache_decode_ops 5.2e4
kv_cache_hit_ratio 0.74
request_streaming_stalls_total 320 (5m)
request_p99_latency 2.42
```

Jessica Hart: looks like evictions >> prefill. Could be fragmentation / hot-prefix churn. If prefill is cheap we might prefill more, but decode load is high so prefill vs decode imbalance causing eviction storms.

Ryan Zhou: agree. On runtime we've seen a case where very large concurrent context windows + prefix churn cause frequent small-entry evictions and tail latency spikes.

Maria Garcia: immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce prefill concurrency for this pool (limit to 25%) 2) bump KV cache memory cap for pool by 20% 3) enable temporary conservative eviction policy (LRU -> size-aware LRU) 4) route traffic for top-affected customers to fallback model variant (lower memory). I'll start 1 & 2.

Sam Kim: executing step 1: applying runtime flag:```
# disable aggressive prefill for pool 3
curl -X POST -d '{"prefill_enabled":false, "prefill_max_concurrency":0.25}' https://controlplane.internal/pools/runtime-pool-us-east-1/flags
```
Sam Kim: response 200. Prefill ops dropped to ~2k in next 1m.

ops-bot: scaling pool runtime-pool-us-east-1 from 12 -> 16 nodes (API request accepted).

Maria Garcia: bumping KV cache memory cap for the pool via infra API:```
POST /infra/pools/runtime-pool-us-east-1/cache/resize
{"memory_mb": 46080} # +20%
```
Maria Garcia: resize initiated, rolling restart of workers will happen over 6m.

Asha (CS): quick heads-up — CS reports two customers saw streaming stalls: AcmeCorp (internal product search) and Flowly (chat). CS is sending status. Estimated customer impact: ~3-8% of requests experienced degraded streaming, a few timed out and retried.

Sam Kim: after prefill change and scale, metrics 8m later:```
kv_cache_evictions_total 4.3k -> 600 (5m)
kv_cache_hit_ratio 0.74 -> 0.90
request_p99_latency 2.42 -> 1.18
request_streaming_stalls_total 320 -> 12
```
Sam Kim: p99 back under SLO but still watch for regressions.

Jessica Hart: good. We should also investigate root cause: why prefill ops were so high relative to decode. Hypothesis: a small number of customers sending large amounts of unique prefixes causing fragmentation and small objects filling LRU. Need a replay of a sample trace & core dump KV layout.

Maria Garcia: ticketing follow-up: create incident (#INC-196250). Collect: heap snapshots, KV metrics per-prefix, sample requests for top 10 prefixes by eviction count, and runtime GC logs. I'll start the collection.

Ryan Zhou: next steps for oncall postmortem: 1) add protective backpressure on prefill when evictions/sec > threshold 2) add metric alert for kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio 3) evaluate size-aware eviction default for heavy pools 4) better customer routing to fallback variants.

Sam Kim: I'm handing off to Ryan for the night. Monitoring dashboard link: https://dashboards.internal/d/runtime/pool/us-east-1 (watch p99, evictions, prefill ops). If evictions rise above 500/min or p99 > 1.5s re-escalate to eng-runtime.

Sam Kim: notes added to incident channel and incident ticket. :white_check_mark:

Ryan Zhou: taking over. Oncall handoff: I'll monitor for next 6h, will coordinate with Eng Runtime tomorrow for a proper fix. Ryan -> logging into oncall pager.

Asha (CS): I'll send a short customer note to AcmeCorp & Flowly: "We observed transient streaming degradation between 14:05-14:30 UTC due to cache pressure. We mitigated by throttling prefill and adding capacity; impacts were reduced soon after. We will follow up with root cause analysis."

Maria Garcia: final note in thread: please add any additional symptoms or logs to INC-196250. We'll schedule a postmortem once root causes are confirmed. Thanks all. :pray:
